title: Crown grazing lease terms
finding: The grazing lease's own terms govern what forest work it allows, and older leases differ.

actions.description: Record the Crown lands file, signed lease and management plan. Check the legal boundary, current term, timber reservation, consent wording, access, forage and range improvements.

title: Review the proposal with the grazing lessee
finding: Provincial grazing policy reserves the timber to the Crown but asks that harvest let the lessee meet the lease management plan, and that harvest, silviculture, site preparation and roads be reviewed with the lessee first.

actions.description: Record the review with the lessee, what was agreed or objected to, and any deposit for range improvements. For a lease issued before November 2004, read the lease itself for the lessee's rights.

title: Lease restriction or consent withheld
finding: Under the grazing policy, where an older lease requires consent and the lessee withholds it, timber rights are not granted over the leasehold until the lease is replaced or amended; for other leases the dispute goes to the Crown land manager.

actions.description: Record the exact clause, whether the lease predates November 2004, and the status of consent, referral or amendment with the Crown land administrator.
Where the lease requires consent, obtain it in writing before planning harvest or silviculture on the leasehold.

title: Land Act reserve, withdrawal or designated use area
finding: A Land Act reserve (§15), withdrawal (§16) or designated use area (§17) withholds the land from disposition under the Land Act; a §17 designation only from dispositions the minister finds incompatible with its purpose, and the minister may set terms on the land's use (§17(1.1)). None of the three refers to forest practices or lifts the FRPA §29 duty, and a designated area is not leased land, so a Range Act agreement can cover it.

actions.description: Record the Crown lands file, document number, purpose and effective date (GATOR, by file number with tenure history on), and obtain the signed notice, its terms and any land use report. Under the 2021 Crown land policy a §17 designation's standard term is 10 years, up to 30 with a review every 5; an expiry of 9999 is a record to ask the land manager about, not a term.

title: Designation terms that restrict the forest work
finding: The designation's own terms restrict the proposed harvest or reforestation. Whether a Land Act term binds a timber sale licence or the FRPA stocking standard is for the land manager and the district to settle before the block proceeds.

actions.description: Record the exact term, who holds the designation, and the land manager's and district's answer on how it applies to the harvest and to the plan's stocking standard.
Where the terms make harvesting or planting incompatible, obtain the designation holder's agreement, an amendment of the designation, or a changed footprint before scheduling the block.

title: A designated use area is not a lease
finding: A §17 grazing designation is not a lease and not a Range Act agreement. FPPR §44(3)(d) turns on a Range Act agreement over the land and its exclusive use for grazing or hay, never on the designation alone.

actions.description: Record the Range Act agreement that covers the harvested ground and the evidence that the ground will be used exclusively for grazing or hay under it.

title: Grazing or hay agreement and approved range plan
finding: Review the governing range plan and dates alongside the forestry activity.

actions.description: Record the RAN file, agreement, approved range use or stewardship plan or documented exception, pasture boundaries, grazing or hay schedule, and range developments.

title: Livestock kept off a regenerating stand
finding: Grazing and reforestation share the ground: a range agreement holder who knows grazing will significantly interfere with establishing the free-growing stand must remove the livestock from the area and keep them out, unless the minister exempts the holder from keeping them out once measures prevent it recurring.

actions.description: Tell the range agreement holder where and when the stand is to be established, and record the range plan's pastures and seasons over the block.
Agree the measures (fencing, timing, herding) with the range agreement holder and the district, and record who carries each.

exceptions.label: The land is, or will be, used exclusively for grazing livestock or cutting hay under a Range Act agreement (FPPR §44(3)(d)); never on land leased under the Land Act, which is not Crown range (Range Act §1)
evidence: The Range Act agreement and its range use plan over the area
The mapped footprint of the exclusive use, confirmed with the district
That no Land Act lease covers the ground

exceptions.label: Harvesting is restricted to a purpose FPPR §44(3)(a)–(c), (f) or (g) lists: eliminating a safety hazard, collecting seed with an opening of 1 ha or less, removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way, clearing for a recreation site or trail, or felling trees treated to trap pests
evidence: The purpose, and that harvesting is restricted to it
For seed collection, the opening’s area

exceptions.label: Harvesting is restricted to commercial thinning, removal of individual trees or similar intermediate cutting, or to special forest products (FPPR §44(3)(h)–(i)); for 12 months after harvest the area must conform to the plan’s §16(4) stocking standard (§44(4))
evidence: The prescription and the stand left after harvest
The plan’s §16(4) stocking standard, and the stand checked against it over the 12 months after harvest

exceptions.label: The minister, satisfied that measures prevent the interference recurring, has exempted the range agreement holder from keeping the livestock out (RPPR §44(2)); removing them still stands
evidence: The measures taken
The minister’s exemption

title: Range development on Crown range
finding: Removing, damaging, modifying or building a range development on Crown range needs the minister's written authorization.

actions.description: Obtain the minister's written authorization before the work, and record its conditions.
Record each fence, gate, cattle guard or water development the work touches, with the range agreement holder responsible for it.

title: Natural range barrier impact
finding: A practice that removes or renders ineffective a natural range barrier must be followed by the mitigation the operational plan specifies or the minister authorizes.

actions.description: Carry out the plan's measure (FPPR §18 requires a forest stewardship plan to specify one) or a measure the minister authorizes, with its timing and who is responsible.
Record evidence that the feature stops or significantly impedes livestock movement, the range holder's response, and whether a permit issued before the plan expired carries the duty forward (§48(2)).

title: Restriction in the applicable forest plan
finding: The holder must achieve the plan's results and carry out its strategies, so a plan clause that restricts the activity binds it.

actions.description: Record the approved plan, amendment and clause. Check whether retaining the barrier, changing the footprint or timing, carrying out the required step, or a plan amendment resolves the conflict.

title: The forest plan carries the ADA/SRA order
finding: The forest stewardship plan's own result or strategy for ADAs and SRAs binds the holder, alongside the order itself.

actions.description: Record the plan's clause and any added commitment (one published plan in the district also caps permanent access at 7% of a block's gross area).

title: Permit in effect when the order took effect
finding: Part II says the order does not affect this permit, licence, area or range schedule; the rest of the review still applies.

actions.description: Record the permit or schedule and its date against the order's Gazette date.

title: No harvest pathway under the order
provision: I, Parts A, B and E
finding: The order allows harvest in an ADA or SRA only for environmental and safety reasons (Part A), forest health (Part B) or a deviation the agriculture ministry determines (Part E). With none of them, the proposal has no harvest pathway under the order. That is the reading taken: the order manages timber subject to Parts A to E and names no other harvest, without saying so in those words.

actions.description: Leave the block out of the schedule, redraw it outside the ADA or SRA, or ask the agriculture ministry about a Part E deviation.

title: Environmental or safety harvest

when.value: Part A: environmental or safety harvest

finding: Part A needs a proposal by local or provincial government, agreement between the forests and agriculture ministries, and an operational work plan directing the harvest.

actions.description: Record the proposing government, the interagency agreement and the operational work plan.

title: Forest-health basis for the harvest
finding: Part B needs a clear indication that the sanitation harvest will significantly assist in preventing the spread of a forest health problem to adjacent stands.

actions.description: Record the forest health survey, the pest and the adjacent stands at risk.

title: Dead or infested timber only
finding: Under Part B only dead or infested timber is removed; live or non-infested trees are taken only where access, skidding or safety needs them.

actions.description: Redraw the block or prescription to take only dead or infested timber, and record each exception's operational reason.

title: Conditions on a forest-health harvest
finding: Each Part C condition applies to a Part B harvest.

actions.description: Leave stumps at least 15 cm high except where access, skidding, landings or safety need them lower; pile logging waste and burn or remove it, never spread it; minimize permanent access, gravelling included, and place it along lot lines and natural boundaries.

title: Referral to the agriculture ministry
finding: Every harvesting proposal under Part B is to be referred to the agriculture ministry.

actions.description: Refer the harvesting proposal to the agriculture ministry and record the referral and its response.

title: No site preparation or planting after a forest-health harvest
finding: Part C.5 rules out site preparation and artificial regeneration for a Part B harvest, so the stand must come back naturally.

actions.description: Take site preparation, planting and seeding out of the silviculture prescription, or record a Part E deviation the agriculture ministry determined that allows them.

title: Planting after an environmental or safety harvest

when.value: Part A: environmental or safety harvest

finding: Part C, including C.5, applies only to Part B harvests, so the order does not bar site preparation or planting after a Part A harvest. The operational work plan Part A requires may still say how the ground is to be left.

actions.description: Record what the operational work plan and the interagency agreement say about regeneration of the harvested ground.

title: Deviation from the order

when.value: Part E: deviation determined by the agriculture ministry

finding: A Part E deviation is limited and conditional salvage or harvest determined by the agriculture ministry and administered by the forests ministry, or an adjustment for Crown land adjudication.

actions.description: Record the agriculture ministry's determination, its conditions and which of Parts A to D it departs from, including whether it allows planting.

title: No new area-based forest tenure
finding: Part D says no area-based forest tenure will be established in these ADAs and SRAs.

actions.description: Keep the ADA or SRA out of the proposed tenure area, or record a Part E deviation.

title: Free-growing stand after harvest
finding: The holder must establish a free-growing stand on the net area to be reforested, to the plan’s stocking standards and dates, unless an exception this rule lists relieves it.

actions.description: Record the timber authority, applicable plan and stocking standard, planting or natural regeneration method, regeneration and free-growing dates, and any approved transfer of the duty (§29.1).

exceptions.label: Harvesting is restricted to a purpose FPPR §44(3)(a)–(c), (f) or (g) lists: eliminating a safety hazard, collecting seed with an opening of 1 ha or less, removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way, clearing for a recreation site or trail, or felling trees treated to trap pests
evidence: The purpose, and that harvesting is restricted to it
For seed collection, the opening’s area

exceptions.label: Harvesting is restricted to experimental purposes that, in the minister’s opinion, will be carried out under controlled scientific or investigative conditions (FPPR §44(3)(e))
evidence: The experiment’s design
The minister’s opinion that its conditions are controlled

exceptions.label: The land is, or will be, used exclusively for grazing livestock or cutting hay under a Range Act agreement (FPPR §44(3)(d)); never on land leased under the Land Act, which is not Crown range (Range Act §1)
evidence: The Range Act agreement and its range use plan over the area
The mapped footprint of the exclusive use, confirmed with the district
That no Land Act lease covers the ground

exceptions.label: Harvesting is restricted to commercial thinning, removal of individual trees or similar intermediate cutting, or to special forest products (FPPR §44(3)(h)–(i)); for 12 months after harvest the area must conform to the plan’s §16(4) stocking standard (§44(4))
evidence: The prescription and the stand left after harvest
The plan’s §16(4) stocking standard, and the stand checked against it over the 12 months after harvest

exceptions.label: The minister, satisfied that the duty is not practicable given the circumstances or conditions of the area, has exempted the holder from FRPA §29 (FPPR §91(1)(a))
evidence: The written exemption, what it covers and when it takes effect, filed with the district office

title: Cannot reforest a forest-health harvest in an ADA or SRA
provision: 29 with the 2006 order Part C.5 and FPPR 44(3)
finding: On these answers the block cannot be both harvested under Part B and reforested as FRPA §29 requires: Part C.5 rules out site preparation and planting, and natural regeneration is not expected to meet the stocking standard by its regeneration date. Only an exception this rule lists changes that.

actions.description: Before scheduling the harvest, change the footprint or prescription so natural regeneration can meet the standard, leave the block out, record evidence that it will, or ask the district whether the agricultural ground can be reserved for purposes other than timber harvesting, which takes it out of the net area to be reforested (FPPR §1(2)). Check that the plan has a stocking standard (FPPR §16) for naturally regenerated Part B blocks, and whether a removal of individual dead trees from a living stand would instead be an intermediate cut (FPPR §44(3)(h)).
Ask the agriculture ministry whether a Part E deviation allowing planting applies, and record its determination.

exceptions.label: Harvesting is restricted to commercial thinning, removal of individual trees or similar intermediate cutting, or to special forest products (FPPR §44(3)(h)–(i)); for 12 months after harvest the area must conform to the plan’s §16(4) stocking standard (§44(4))
evidence: The prescription and the stand left after harvest
The plan’s §16(4) stocking standard, and the stand checked against it over the 12 months after harvest

exceptions.label: The land is, or will be, used exclusively for grazing livestock or cutting hay under a Range Act agreement (FPPR §44(3)(d)); never on land leased under the Land Act, which is not Crown range (Range Act §1)
evidence: The Range Act agreement and its range use plan over the area
The mapped footprint of the exclusive use, confirmed with the district
That no Land Act lease covers the ground

exceptions.label: The agriculture ministry has determined a Part E deviation from Parts A to D that allows site preparation or planting
evidence: The ministry’s determination and its conditions

exceptions.label: The minister, satisfied that the duty is not practicable given the circumstances or conditions of the area, has exempted the holder from FRPA §29 (FPPR §91(1)(a))
evidence: The written exemption, what it covers and when it takes effect, filed with the district office

title: Ground reserved from the net area to be reforested
finding: Areas reserved for purposes other than timber harvesting are excluded from the net area to be reforested, so the free-growing duty does not reach the reserved ground; the rest of the cutblock keeps it.

actions.description: Record where the reservation is made (cutting permit, site plan or the district's direction), its purpose and its mapped area, and confirm with the district that it is a reservation the definition covers.

title: Permanent grazing opening in the reforestation area
finding: Keeping part of the net area to be reforested open for grazing conflicts with the free-growing duty, which applies to each hectare of it, unless an exception this rule lists applies.

actions.description: Before harvest, take the opening out of the net area to be reforested only where the plan and the district allow it, or confirm a Range Act agreement and exclusive use that would support FPPR §44(3)(d). Verify clearing authority for the same footprint.

exceptions.label: The standards unit otherwise conforms to its stocking standard, and each opening is under 1 ha, or the mappable openings of 1 to 2 ha take no more than 5% of the unit (FPPR §46.11(2))
evidence: The openings mapped within the standards unit, with their areas
The unit’s stocking survey

exceptions.label: The forest stewardship plan specifies otherwise than that the duty is met on each hectare of the net area to be reforested (FPPR §46.11(1))
exceptions.decidedBy: The minister, approving the forest stewardship plan
evidence: The plan’s provision and its approval

exceptions.label: The land is, or will be, used exclusively for grazing livestock or cutting hay under a Range Act agreement (FPPR §44(3)(d)); never on land leased under the Land Act, which is not Crown range (Range Act §1)
evidence: The Range Act agreement and its range use plan over the area
The mapped footprint of the exclusive use, confirmed with the district
That no Land Act lease covers the ground

exceptions.label: The minister, satisfied that the duty is not practicable given the circumstances or conditions of the area, has exempted the holder from FRPA §29 (FPPR §91(1)(a))
evidence: The written exemption, what it covers and when it takes effect, filed with the district office

title: Exemption from the free-growing duty by the minister
finding: With no reserved ground, leaving the net area unreforested needs an exemption from FRPA §29, which the minister may grant only if satisfied that the duty is not practicable given the circumstances or conditions of the particular area. It must be in writing, say what it covers and when it takes effect, and be filed with the district office. A §44(3) purpose, listed as this rule’s exceptions, needs no exemption.

actions.description: Apply to the district for a §91 exemption before harvest, with the evidence that establishing a free-growing stand is not practicable on that ground (site, grazing, the range plan, past openings nearby), and keep the written exemption with the site plan.
Record nearby openings that were reforested under the same conditions: they bear on whether the duty is practicable.

exceptions.label: Harvesting is restricted to a purpose FPPR §44(3)(a)–(c), (f) or (g) lists: eliminating a safety hazard, collecting seed with an opening of 1 ha or less, removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way, clearing for a recreation site or trail, or felling trees treated to trap pests
evidence: The purpose, and that harvesting is restricted to it
For seed collection, the opening’s area

exceptions.label: Harvesting is restricted to experimental purposes that, in the minister’s opinion, will be carried out under controlled scientific or investigative conditions (FPPR §44(3)(e))
evidence: The experiment’s design
The minister’s opinion that its conditions are controlled

exceptions.label: The land is, or will be, used exclusively for grazing livestock or cutting hay under a Range Act agreement (FPPR §44(3)(d)); never on land leased under the Land Act, which is not Crown range (Range Act §1)
evidence: The Range Act agreement and its range use plan over the area
The mapped footprint of the exclusive use, confirmed with the district
That no Land Act lease covers the ground

title: An existing opening that cannot meet its standard
finding: A person who knows a free-growing stand cannot be established to the applicable standard must notify the minister with the reasons and submit a proposal for establishing one (stocking standards, free-growing height and latest date). The minister must approve it if it is consistent with FPPR §26(3); a rejection is reviewable.

actions.description: Give notice and submit the proposal to the district, and record the approval or the written reasons for a rejection.

title: A Land Act lease is not Crown range
finding: The Range Act grants grazing and hay rights only over Crown range, which excludes Crown land leased under the Land Act. On leased ground, FPPR §44(3)(d) cannot relieve the free-growing duty.

actions.description: Separate the leased ground from any Range Act tenure on the map, and plan the leased ground's reforestation under FRPA §29 unless another basis applies.
